text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING @oncall (alex) — elevated alerts: customer=Evros (private VPC, dedicated pool). Upstream OIDC JWKS fetch failing across their tenant. Errors: 502/504 and "'x509: certificate has expired'" reported by identity-proxy. Impact: auth failures for API traffic, ~20% of requests getting 401/502. Please triage.

alex: acked, I'm on it. grabbing logs from the identity-proxy and the dedicated gateway. Can someone post the last 5m of jwks fetch errors? @infra-ops-bot?

infra-ops-bot: recent logs from gw-evros-01 (tail):
```
2026-03-15T09:12:04Z ERROR jwks-fetch: GET https://jwks.evros.internal/.well-known/jwks.json -> x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z WARN auth: token-exchange failed user=svc-account-42 err="jwks fetch failed"
2026-03-15T09:13:16Z ERROR proxy: upstream 502 when validating assertion
```

alex: thanks. evros-sre — are you seeing any cert rotations on your side? thumbprint mismatch maybe?

evros-sre: hi all — we started a cert rotation earlier this morning but the rollout didn't finish. Some hosts are still serving the old cert which expired at 09:10 UTC. We pushed a fix to their load balancer but because this is a private VPC behind their firewall, the cert bundle in our identity-proxy wasn't updated. We're coordinating with their infra now.

maria: if the proxied JWKS endpoint presents an expired TLS cert, the identity-proxy will refuse the connection (default TLS verify). Two options: 1) rotate/finish customer's cert ASAP (preferred), or 2) temporarily use a cached JWKS copy or a regional mirror to allow auth while we avoid disabling TLS verification. I'm against disabling TLS verify (too risky).

kevin: agree with Maria. We have a previously cached JWKS snapshot for Evros from 02:55 UTC. Can we flip a tenant-level fallback to use the cached JWKS for 10m while Evros completes rotation?

alex: yes. Steps I propose:
1) enable tenant fallback to cached JWKS (10m window) for evros-tenant in config service
2) patch routing so dedicated pool gw nodes read fallback first then try live fetch (non-blocking)
3) ask Evros to finish LB cert rollout and confirm thumbprint
4) monitor error rate and rollback fallback after stable

kevin: I'm patching the config now. Applying feature flag: `evros_jwks_fallback=true` for tenant evros-tenant. CLI:
```
redwood-cli tenant-patch evros-tenant --set jwks_fallback=true --ttl 600
```

infra-ops-bot: feature flag applied, patched gw-evros-01..04 to read fallback. Live: 2026-03-15T09:18:22Z

alex: rolling quick canary on gw-evros-01 -> gw-evros-02, monitoring auth latency and 401 rate.

diane: customer impact update from Evros: their SSO portal shows users being kicked out; SRE reports spike in support tickets. They estimate ~12% of transactions fail intermittently since 09:08 UTC. If fallback reduces failures, we can avoid a full outage.

alex: metrics after fallback (09:20 UTC): 401 rate down from 18% to 3% for auth traffic. Latency unchanged. Good. Keeping fallback for now. @evros-sre, can you confirm when all LB nodes present new cert?

evros-sre: confirmed — rotation completed at 09:26 UTC. Thumbprint: SHA256:AB:12:34:... We restarted their OIDC service for good measure. They also uploaded the intermediate into chain. We expect TLS handshake to succeed now.

maria: verifying from our side with `openssl` to their internal endpoint over the tunnel:
```
openssl s_client -connect jwks.evros.internal:443 -showcerts -servername jwks.evros.internal
# output shows valid cert issued 2026-02-15 -> 2027-02-15
```
TLS handshake OK.

alex: patching tenant to disable fallback. CLI:
```
redwood-cli tenant-patch evros-tenant --set jwks_fallback=false
```

infra-ops-bot: remove feature flag, gw-evros nodes reverted to live JWKS fetch at 09:31:18Z

alex: monitoring post-change. Auth 401s remain <1% over 5m. We'll keep an eye for the next hour. Root cause: incomplete cert rotation on customer LB exposed expired cert to our identity-proxy. Contributing factor: no automated health-check for JWKS TLS cert expiry in the private VPC probe.

kevin: filing short follow-ups: (1) add JWKS TLS expiry watcher for tenant config (ticket INF-1242), (2) document safe fallback procedure in runbook (RB-853), (3) add tenant-level alert when cached-fallback is used (so ops are aware).

diane: customer-facing comms: I drafted a message to Evros SRE: "Thanks for quick fix. We used a temporary cached-JWKS fallback to keep traffic healthy while you completed rotation. Recommend automating post-rotation healthcheck and share rotation windows with Redwood SRE for future planned rotations." Evros approved.

alex: handing off to @maria for overnight monitoring. If rates creep above 2% reopen paging.

maria: ack — I'll take over until 2026-03-16T02:00 UTC. Posting followups to postmortem template and assigning owners. Good job team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident closed -> severity: P2, duration: ~23min, mitigation: cached jwks fallback, permanent fix: INF-1242, RB-853 assigned.
